sections.heading: The partnership opportunity
paragraphs: Ginza Natsuno is a Tokyo chopstick specialist introduced through Japan Industrial Promotion Inc. (JIP Japan) to buyers outside Japan. The opportunity is a distribution or export relationship in which a partner brings Japanese craft chopsticks and related tableware to hospitality, retail or gifting customers in its own market.

The company already serves corporate customers in Japan with custom, engraved and promotional chopsticks, and it ships internationally through its online shop. A distribution partner would extend that into trade channels such as hotel supply, department store counters and corporate gift programmes.

sections.heading: About Ginza Natsuno
paragraphs: Ginza Natsuno opened its first shop in Ginza, Tokyo, in May 1999 and describes itself as a chopstick specialist, with the aim of preserving Japanese chopstick culture and supporting regional craftspeople. Its main store is at Ginza 6-chome, Chuo-ku, and further stores operate in Tokyo and other cities.
Besides retail, the company runs chopstick-making workshops where visitors shape wood by hand, which reflects a focus on explaining how the products are made.

sections.heading: Products
paragraphs: The range covers roughly 2,500 to 3,000 designs of chopsticks sourced from craft regions across Japan, in materials and finishes such as lacquered wood, mother-of-pearl inlay and natural wood. Over 1,000 chopstick rests, bowls, lacquerware and other Japanese tableware complete the offer.
Engraved names and custom designs are part of the service, which suits gifting, weddings, commemorative items and branded hospitality use.

sections.heading: Expansion plans and target markets
paragraphs: The stated target is international markets, with a focus on luxury hotels, restaurants, department stores, gift distributors and specialist retailers. Specific countries, volumes and timelines are not published and are discussed after a qualified inquiry.

sections.heading: Who the ideal partner is
paragraphs: A suitable partner already sells to hospitality, premium retail or corporate gifting and can present Japanese craft products with context on origin and use. Experience with tableware, lacquerware, giftware or Japanese cultural goods is relevant, as is the ability to handle import compliance and after-sales communication locally.

sections.heading: Commercial and regulatory considerations
paragraphs: Terms such as pricing, minimum order quantities, territory and exclusivity are not published and are discussed after a qualified inquiry. Lacquered and wooden products that may touch food are subject to food-contact material rules in the importing country, so partners should confirm local requirements and documentation with the supplier before ordering.

sections.heading: Why this opportunity
paragraphs: The supplier is a long-standing specialist with a deep product range and an existing corporate service, so a partner can select assortments for different channels rather than a single product line. The introduction through JIP Japan gives international buyers a structured first contact.
